writeup.headline: AngloGold Ashanti rates Buy on very strong revenue growth, held back by weak price trend and mixed news.
writeup.thesis: AngloGold Ashanti scores 67, a Buy, but only three of six factors could be scored, so growth, trend and news carry the whole rating. Growth scores 100, with TTM revenue growth of 70.8% and growth sped up by 44.4 pp from the previous quarter. The trend factor scores 39: the price is 13.0% below its 50-day average, 10.0% below its 200-day average and 32.0% below its 52-week high, even though shares are up 53.3% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago. News risk is neutral at 50, as a JSE censure over a late results announcement offsets positive commentary on the Arthur project in Nevada. Quality, balance sheet and valuation are unscored, though gross margin is 49.2% and cash to debt is 1.49.
key_risks: The score is only 3 points above the Hold threshold, so a small slip in any factor could cut the rating.
Weak recent price action: shares are 10.4 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days and 32.0% below their 52-week high.
Diluted share count up 18.1% year on year, which dilutes per-share gains from revenue growth.
Operational setbacks, including flooding at Iduapriem and a fatality at Obuasi, could threaten the ~3.0Moz 2026 production guidance.
Revenue growth this strong likely depends on gold prices, so a gold price fall could reverse the growth score.
what_would_change: A drop of 3 points in the score, for example from further price weakness pushing the trend score lower or a slowdown in revenue growth, would move the rating down to Hold.
Reaching Strong Buy needs 13 more points, most plausibly from a recovering share price lifting the trend score from 39.
Verified positive news, such as confirmed analyst upgrades or progress on Arthur, could lift the news risk score from 50; new regulatory issues would lower it.
Once quality, balance sheet and valuation can be scored, they could move the composite either way.
